articles.headline: ‘Everyone wants to make history’: revamped Huanggang Port opens to brisk business

articles.takeaway: Hong Kong travel agencies and border shops have capitalised on the opening of the revamped Huanggang Port as thousands of visitors poured through the control point, with special tours on offer and shopkeepers reporting…
body: Hong Kong travel agencies and border shops have capitalised on the opening of the revamped Huanggang Port as thousands of visitors poured through the control point, with special tours on offer and shopkeepers reporting brisk business.
Agents said the port’s 24-hour joint clearance arrangements could give cross-border tourism a major boost, although crowd control measures dampened trade at the checkpoint entrance.

Tour groups organised by Hong Kong travel agency Big Line Holiday were among the first visitors at the upgraded checkpoint on Monday morning. Chan Yin-ping, the agency’s chairwoman, said about 1,000 people had joined the tours, with 20 groups scheduled between 10am and 1pm.

Plans for further tours had yet to be decided, pending a smooth first few days of operation. The agency staggered the tours across different time slots to avoid putting too much pressure on the new checkpoint.
“But we still decided to organise the tours because today is the first day and everyone wants to make history,” she said. Chan was confident the port would give tourism a boost.

“The port is open 24 hours and Shenzhen is just across the border from the New Territories, unlike the round-the-clock crossing at the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macau Bridge, which involves a much longer journey,” she said.

articles.dek: This is a special contribution from the Centre on Contemporary China and the World at the University of Hong Kong. Read the full report at the end of the article.
articles.lead: This is a special contribution from the Centre on Contemporary China and the World at the University of Hong Kong. Read the full report at the end of the article.
articles.takeaway: This is a special contribution from the Centre on Contemporary China and the World at the University of Hong Kong.
body: This is a special contribution from the Centre on Contemporary China and the World at the University of Hong Kong. Read the full report at the end of the article.

It will be available on the institute website cccw.hku.hk from October 13. With the rising strategic significance of energy, especially due to the need to support China’s artificial intelligence (AI) development, members of the Communist Party’s 20th Central Committee with energy backgrounds – the country’s “movers and shakers” in this strategic sector – merit closer attention.

Among them are former or current power-company executives, petroleum managers, nuclear-safety officials and specialists in water administration. Many built their expertise over decades, establishing themselves as energy technocrats before taking on responsibilities beyond their original industries.

Their biographies reveal a recurring route into political leadership – deep specialisation first and diversification of political experience later, highlighting the growing presence and power of this leadership cohort.

More experience, greater representation Our data set identifies 34 energy sector members, including 21 full members and 13 alternates. They account for 10.2 per cent of the 205 full members, 7.6 per cent of the 171 alternates and 9 per cent of the combined membership.
Three of them were elected to the Politburo in October 2022, representing 12.5 per cent of its 24 members. As of this year, their median ages are 64 among full members and 60 among alternates.

articles.headline: Hong Kong and Shenzhen Forge Deeper Ties in Gold Trade
articles.dek: An integration of Hong Kong's financial infrastructure and Shenzhen's manufacturing prowess aims to create a dominant global gold trading hub.
articles.lead: Hong Kong is enhancing its role as an international gold trading center, leveraging its tax-free status and expanding vaulting capacity. The city aims to increase its physical gold storage to 2,000 tonnes by 2028, supporting both national financial needs and China's substantial consumer demand for gold.
articles.takeaway: An integration of Hong Kong's financial infrastructure and Shenzhen's manufacturing prowess aims to create a dominant global gold trading hub.
body: Hong Kong is enhancing its role as an international gold trading center, leveraging its tax-free status and expanding vaulting capacity. The city aims to increase its physical gold storage to 2,000 tonnes by 2028, supporting both national financial needs and China's substantial consumer demand for gold.

This ambition is increasingly intertwined with Shenzhen's emergence as a major wholesale jewelry and fabrication hub. Shenzhen's Shuibei market, now Asia's largest by volume, handles significant gold trading and is identified in its five-year plan as a competitive industry.

The collaboration allows Shenzhen's jewelry manufacturers to access gold from Hong Kong, fabricate products, and export them efficiently. This process benefits from Hong Kong's offshore gold leasing and Shenzhen's bonded zones, minimizing customs duties and mitigating price fluctuation risks for manufacturers.

New initiatives like Hong Kong's Delivery Connect facilitate the movement of physical gold between the Hong Kong and Shanghai Gold Exchanges, which have vaults in Shenzhen. This integration is expected to make it easier for Shenzhen merchants to lease gold and capitalize on price differentials.

As Hong Kong develops yuan-denominated gold financial products, it will offer Shenzhen jewelers more tools for hedging and risk management. This synergy aims to create a comprehensive gold trading ecosystem, combining finance, wholesale, manufacturing, and retail across both cities.

articles.dek: Court of Appeal upholds decision to acquit former lawmaker Lam Cheuk-ting of perverting the course of justice related to 2019 protests.
articles.lead: Hong Kong's Department of Justice has failed in its appeal against the acquittal of former lawmaker Lam Cheuk-ting. The Court of Appeal on Friday upheld a lower court's decision to find Lam and two co-defendants not guilty of charges stemming from a confrontation in July 2019.
articles.takeaway: Court of Appeal upholds decision to acquit former lawmaker Lam Cheuk-ting of perverting the course of justice related to 2019 protests.
body: Hong Kong's Department of Justice has failed in its appeal against the acquittal of former lawmaker Lam Cheuk-ting. The Court of Appeal on Friday upheld a lower court's decision to find Lam and two co-defendants not guilty of charges stemming from a confrontation in July 2019.

Lam was accused of pressuring a man, identified in court as X, to delete images from his phone. Protesters had suspected X of taking close-up photos of demonstrators during a protest outside the police headquarters in Wan Chai.

In January 2023, a District Court judge had acquitted the defendants of most charges, stating Lam was acting as a peacemaker to de-escalate a tense situation. The judges on Friday agreed, noting that while deleting pictures could obstruct investigations, there was no confirmation the pictures actually existed.
Lam, a former member of the now-defunct Democratic Party, is currently serving a prison sentence after being convicted in the Hong Kong 47 national security case in May 2024.

articles.dek: The new Huanggang checkpoint, described as a 'landmark project' and the world's largest single-building land control point, aims to significantly enhance connectivity and efficiency between Hong Kong and mainland China.
articles.lead: Hong Kong's Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu has hailed the revamped Huanggang Port as a "critical milestone" for the Greater Bay Area's connectivity. The new facility, a joint project between Hong Kong and Shenzhen, is set to open on Monday, replacing the existing Lok Ma Chau/Huanggang crossing which has been in operation for nearly 40 years.
articles.takeaway: The new Huanggang checkpoint, described as a 'landmark project' and the world's largest single-building land control point, aims to significantly enhance connectivity and efficiency between Hong Kong and mainland China.
body: Hong Kong's Chief Executive John Lee Ka-chiu has hailed the revamped Huanggang Port as a "critical milestone" for the Greater Bay Area's connectivity. The new facility, a joint project between Hong Kong and Shenzhen, is set to open on Monday, replacing the existing Lok Ma Chau/Huanggang crossing which has been in operation for nearly 40 years.

The revamped port is designed to handle a daily capacity of 200,000 passenger trips, with potential to increase to 300,000 upon completion of the MTR's Northern Link project. This upgrade is expected to streamline the flow of people, goods, capital, and information between Hong Kong and Shenzhen, fostering deeper integration within the Greater Bay Area.

Officials anticipate a significant increase in daily passenger traffic, with initial estimates suggesting between 100,000 to 200,000 passenger trips per day, up from the current average of 40,000. The new checkpoint will also have a daily capacity of 15,000 vehicles, compared to the previous 9,000.

Implemented under a "collaborative inspection and joint clearance" model, the new port aims to reduce clearance times for eligible passengers from approximately 30 minutes to around five minutes. This efficiency is expected to benefit business travellers, visitors, and residents, and facilitate cross-border collaboration in industrial innovation and talent flow.

Shenzhen officials have confirmed that extensive crowd control and security measures are in place, with over 200 rehearsals conducted to ensure a smooth operational launch and to manage anticipated peak travel flows.

articles.headline: New Huanggang Port Crossing Opens with Joint Clearance System
articles.dek: Hong Kong's revamped Huanggang Port launches a 24/7 joint clearance model, streamlining border crossings for residents and mainland Chinese travelers.
articles.lead: The Huanggang Port officially opens on Monday, following over six years of redevelopment. This new 24/7 checkpoint introduces a "joint clearance" model, allowing passengers to complete both departure and entry procedures in a single automated channel.
articles.takeaway: Hong Kong's revamped Huanggang Port launches a 24/7 joint clearance model, streamlining border crossings for residents and mainland Chinese travelers.
body: The Huanggang Port officially opens on Monday, following over six years of redevelopment. This new 24/7 checkpoint introduces a "joint clearance" model, allowing passengers to complete both departure and entry procedures in a single automated channel.

To utilize the "joint clearance" system, both Hong Kong and mainland Chinese residents must register with immigration authorities on both sides. Hong Kong residents can register via various methods, including traveling to the mainland via other checkpoints or registering at the existing Huanggang checkpoint before its closure. Those unable to use the automated channels can still opt for staffed counters.

Travelers arriving at the new port can only use authorized public transport services, including buses, minibuses, and taxis, to reach a public transport interchange. Cross-boundary coach services also serve the revamped facility, with passengers required to alight for immigration clearance.

The "joint clearance" model utilizes 134 e-channel machines, each with three gates, and 68 staffed counters. Authorities estimate this system will reduce clearance times from 30 minutes to approximately five minutes. Residents holding valid home return permits can use either that document or their Hong Kong identity card for the joint clearance process, though carrying both is advised.

Private car drivers eligible for cross-border travel can use a "joint one-stop" vehicle lane. This process involves passing through a customs kiosk and an integrated information collection device that gathers identity and biometric data for authorities on both sides. Drivers with permits for other checkpoints may have restrictions on when they can use the new Huanggang Port.

Future plans include connecting the revamped crossing to a high-speed intercity railway linking Shenzhen, Guangzhou, and Dongguan. In Hong Kong, returning travelers will find an arrival hall on level four, with public transport options available on level two. Only taxis from five premium fleets are permitted to take bookings inside the building, with other ride-hailing services unavailable within the boundary control area.

attribution.originalTitle: How to zoom through new Huanggang Port crossing at Hong Kong’s border

articles.dek: The government will enhance its Green@Community initiative with 24-hour automated collection points and boost clean energy imports, following the decision to abandon the waste-charging scheme.
articles.lead: Hong Kong is set to bolster its community recycling efforts by expanding the Green@Community initiative, introducing round-the-clock automated collection points. body: Hong Kong is set to bolster its community recycling efforts by expanding the Green@Community initiative, introducing round-the-clock automated collection points. This move comes after the government decided to shelve the controversial waste-charging scheme due to significant public opposition. The environmental chief stated that the focus will now shift to strengthening recycling infrastructure and promoting greater public participation.

The Green@Community network, which spans all 18 districts, currently operates over 800 collection points. The initiative has already contributed to a reduction in waste volume by approximately 1,000 tonnes over the past three to four years. The introduction of automated facilities aims to enhance convenience for residents, encouraging increased engagement with recycling.

In addition to recycling, the government plans to increase the import of clean energy from mainland China. Discussions are underway to raise the proportion of zero-carbon electricity imported from the mainland to between 60 and 70 percent. This strategy is expected to help lower local electricity tariffs in the future.

The government also intends to review the permitted profit levels of the city's two power companies when their current control agreements expire in 2033. Plans are in motion to increase transmission capacity and construct new infrastructure to facilitate the import of large volumes of zero-carbon energy.

These environmental initiatives are part of Hong Kong's broader commitment to achieving its binding goals outlined in the city's first five-year plan. These goals include reducing carbon intensity, increasing the use of zero-carbon energy, and improving air and water quality, with the ultimate aim of reaching carbon neutrality.

body: Skip to content Authorities in Hong Kong and Shenzhen have announced that the newly revamped Huanggang border crossing will begin operation next Monday, with an opening ceremony scheduled for Sunday.

An artist’s impression of the new Huanggang Port. File photo: IDA Design Awards. In a notice jointly issued on Friday, Hong Kong’s Security Bureau and Shenzhen’s Office of Port of Entry and Exit announced that the new control point will open at 6.30am on Monday, October 12, providing round-the-clock clearance services for passengers and vehicles.

“Acceptance inspection of the new port building of the Huanggang Port has been completed,” according to the notice. “Following the completion of a series of system tests, trials and emergency drills by both Hong Kong and Shenzhen, it has been confirmed that the port is ready for opening.” As the new control point comes into operation, passenger clearance services at the temporary port building of the Huanggang Port in Shenzhen and the Lok Ma Chau Control Point in Hong Kong will be suspended, the notice added.

Police commissioner Joe Chow also gazetted a notice permitting staff participants of the opening ceremony of the Huanggang Port to enter the Hong Kong side of the control point between 4am and 10pm on Sunday.

Director of Immigration Benson Kwok inspected the border crossing on Friday, the Immigration Department said in a social media post. Photos released by the department showed Kwok inspecting e-Channel terminals.

Director of Immigration Benson Kwok inspects the newly revamped Huanggang Port on October 9, 2026. Photo: Immigration Departmant, via Instagram. The Immigration Department reminded residents to register for the “co-operative inspection and joint clearance” service via the HK e-Channel mobile app so they can use the automated service at Huanggang Port when it opens.

body: Hong Kong's national security police have charged a 52-year-old man with knowingly publishing publications with seditious intent, nearly three months after his unannounced arrest. The charge, under the Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, alleges the man repeatedly posted content online that provoked hatred towards Beijing, the Hong Kong government, and the judiciary.

He appeared in West Kowloon Magistrates’ Courts on Wednesday to face the charge, which carries a maximum penalty of seven years imprisonment. The man was initially arrested on July 9 in Eastern District, but his arrest was not publicly disclosed at the time. The case has been adjourned to December 15 for a plea.

This case marks the second instance in recent months where a national security offense was only made public after a formal charge was laid, deviating from the usual police practice of publicizing such arrests. Last month, a 61-year-old woman was similarly charged with displaying seditious publications outside her home, with her case also revealed only after her court appearance.

The Safeguarding National Security Ordinance, enacted on March 23, 2024, targets offenses including treason, insurrection, sabotage, external interference, sedition, theft of state secrets, and espionage. The ordinance allows for pre-charge detention of up to 16 days, with potential restrictions on lawyer access and penalties up to life imprisonment.

articles.headline: Boy, 13, rescued after climbing onto air-conditioning unit to escape fire in flat
articles.dek: Hong Kong firefighters have rescued a 13-year-old boy who climbed out a window onto the air-conditioning unit to escape a fire that broke out in his flat, while his mother has been arrested on suspicion of child neglect…
articles.lead: Hong Kong firefighters have rescued a 13-year-old boy who climbed out a window onto the air-conditioning unit to escape a fire that broke out in his flat, while his mother has been arrested on suspicion of child neglect.
articles.takeaway: Hong Kong firefighters have rescued a 13-year-old boy who climbed out a window onto the air-conditioning unit to escape a fire that broke out in his flat, while his mother has been arrested on suspicion of child neglect…
body: Hong Kong firefighters have rescued a 13-year-old boy who climbed out a window onto the air-conditioning unit to escape a fire that broke out in his flat, while his mother has been arrested on suspicion of child neglect.
Police received reports at 7.54pm on Wednesday that a fire had broken out in a flat at Tsui To House, one of the blocks of Tsui Ping (North) Estate in Kwun Tong.

Online footage showed the boy, wearing only his underwear, climbing out of a window and onto the condenser unit as thick black smoke filled the flat. Firefighters deployed a ladder to reach the boy and pulled him to safety.

Around 70 residents were evacuated. The blaze was extinguished at about 8.25pm. The boy, who was suspected to be ill from smoke inhalation, was taken to United Christian Hospital in Kwun Tong for treatment.
A preliminary investigation found the fire was caused by a charger in the living room, and police said the incident was not suspicious. Officers later believed the boy had been left home alone.

His 42-year-old mother, surnamed Ho, was arrested for ill-treatment or neglect of a child or young person under her care and detained for investigation. The case is being handled by the Kwun Tong district criminal investigation unit.

articles.headline: Abby Choi's Mother Accuses Ex-Father-in-Law of Clinging to Daughter's Wealth
articles.dek: The mother of slain socialite Abby Choi Tin-fung described her daughter's former father-in-law as a 'cunning old fox' in court, refuting claims about his financial dealings.
articles.lead: The mother of murdered Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi Tin-fung has accused her daughter's former father-in-law, Kwong Kau, of clinging to the family's fortune. Cheung Yin-fa made the statement in the High Court on Thursday.
articles.takeaway: The mother of slain socialite Abby Choi Tin-fung described her daughter's former father-in-law as a 'cunning old fox' in court, refuting claims about his financial dealings.
body: The mother of murdered Hong Kong socialite Abby Choi Tin-fung has accused her daughter's former father-in-law, Kwong Kau, of clinging to the family's fortune. Cheung Yin-fa made the statement in the High Court on Thursday.

Cheung Yin-fa rejected a suggestion from Kwong Kau's lawyer that he had purchased a Rolls-Royce using funds from business activities after his retirement. She told the court that her daughter had provided Kwong Kau with a monthly allowance of HK$20,000.
Furthermore, Cheung Yin-fa stated that Abby Choi had paid over HK$200,000 to cover Kwong Kau's medical expenses during a period when he was ill.

articles.headline: Hong Kong Police Arrest Parents Over Child Abuse Allegations
articles.dek: Parents of an 11-year-old girl filmed carrying dozens of beer cans were arrested on suspicion of child abuse after a video circulated online.
articles.lead: Hong Kong police have arrested the parents of an 11-year-old girl who was filmed struggling to carry dozens of beer cans. The 38-year-old father and 32-year-old mother were detained on suspicion of "ill-treatment or neglect by those in charge of a child or young person," a charge commonly known as child abuse.
articles.takeaway: Parents of an 11-year-old girl filmed carrying dozens of beer cans were arrested on suspicion of child abuse after a video circulated online.
body: Hong Kong police have arrested the parents of an 11-year-old girl who was filmed struggling to carry dozens of beer cans. The 38-year-old father and 32-year-old mother were detained on suspicion of "ill-treatment or neglect by those in charge of a child or young person," a charge commonly known as child abuse.

The arrests followed the circulation of a video showing the girl carrying two dozen beer cans and a damaged schoolbag. She reportedly declined offers of help, stating she feared her father would scold her. The father later appeared, criticized his daughter, and took a bag from her.

Police received a report on Tuesday evening and initially believed the girl had picked up the beer voluntarily. However, the case was reclassified the following afternoon and taken over by the New Territories North Child Abuse Investigation Unit, which initiated a probe and involved the Social Welfare Department.

The parents told local media that the incident was a "misunderstanding" and denied child abuse, claiming the beer-carrying was a motor skills exercise for their daughter, who has a condition affecting physical coordination. They stated all three of their children have special needs and that services in Tuen Mun District are insufficient.

attribution.originalTitle: Hong Kong police arrest parents of 11-year-old girl filmed carrying dozens of beer cans

articles.headline: Huanggang Port Reopens with Strict Transport Rules for Travellers
articles.dek: Hong Kong authorities mandate the use of authorized public transport, including licensed taxis, for access to the revamped Huanggang Port, restricting other ride-hailing services.
articles.lead: Travellers using the newly revamped Huanggang Port will be required to utilize only authorized public transport services. This includes pre-booked licensed taxi fleets, as other ride-hailing services will not be permitted within the boundary control area.
articles.takeaway: Hong Kong authorities mandate the use of authorized public transport, including licensed taxis, for access to the revamped Huanggang Port, restricting other ride-hailing services.
body: Travellers using the newly revamped Huanggang Port will be required to utilize only authorized public transport services. This includes pre-booked licensed taxi fleets, as other ride-hailing services will not be permitted within the boundary control area.

Hong Kong government officials announced these regulations at a press conference on Wednesday. Transport officials also advised travellers against rushing to use the port during its initial operational phase.

The Huanggang Port is expected to reopen in the coming days, following significant renovations. The new transport arrangements aim to manage passenger flow and ensure compliance with regulations within the port's controlled zones.

Further details on the authorized transport services and operational procedures are expected to be released as the opening date approaches. The government emphasized adherence to these rules for a smooth transition.

attribution.originalTitle: Travellers must use authorised buses, taxis at Huanggang Port, Hong Kong authorities say

faqs.question: What type of transport is permitted at Huanggang Port?
faqs.answer: Only authorized public transport services, including pre-booked licensed taxis, are permitted at Huanggang Port.

faqs.question: Are ride-hailing services allowed at Huanggang Port?
faqs.answer: No, other ride-hailing services will not be available inside the boundary control area of Huanggang Port.
